THE_PATTERN_IS_NOW_COMPLETE.reading: Every overlay we have built lands in the same 36 to 39 band once replicated, against a family control of 33.8. None of them is distinguishable from any other, and the first run of each was misleadingly high in all three cases. This is the strongest internal evidence yet for the paper's thesis, and it is decisive for strategy: our overlay programme has plateaued at roughly +3 to +5 levels, which is about +0.2 to +0.3 board points. The gap to rank 3 is +2.0. Overlays cannot close it.
THE_PATTERN_IS_NOW_COMPLETE.consequence: Arms S and T stay in the daily rotation because on a max-keeping board a tie costs exactly nothing and each has a >20.7% prior of being best. But GPU should stop buying more overlays of this class.

WHAT_IS_SIZED_TO_THE_GAP.finding: The recipe that reaches ~100% on these exact 25 games is now published FOUR independent times: Tycho (2026-07-28, Apache-2.0), Twin (2026-08-14, MIT, 179/183 levels at 0.61x human actions), Retrodict (updated 2026-08-22, all 183 levels), and Prime Agent (paper 2026-08-24, MIT). NVIDIA's AVO (2026-08-21) reports 100.00 RHAE with no code. All four converge on the SAME loop.
the_loop: 1. Write an executable Python world model of the game.
2. VALIDATE: refuse to take any scored action until that program reproduces every transition observed so far, exactly.
3. PLAN: search inside the validated model (Twin uses BFS at depth 8, 20,000 nodes).
4. EXECUTE CHECKED: submit the planned actions one at a time, halt at the first misprediction, and turn that mismatch into the repair counterexample.
WHAT_IS_SIZED_TO_THE_GAP.why_it_fits_this_metric_specifically: ARC-AGI-3 scores only environment-changing actions. Internal reasoning and tool calls are FREE. So planning inside a world model converts free compute into scored efficiency, which is exactly what the scorer rewards. And it attacks our measured bottleneck: a median q38 game gets only ~16 model decisions, and this recipe turns one decision into a whole planned action sequence.
WHAT_IS_SIZED_TO_THE_GAP.why_our_old_objection_is_retired: We deferred world models on Tycho's ablation showing an UNVERIFIED world model is WORSE than a textual baseline. The validation gate in step 2 is precisely the missing half. That deferral is retired, not re-litigated.
WHAT_IS_SIZED_TO_THE_GAP.the_prerequisite_and_it_is_already_half_: The duck sandbox rebuilds its globals on every tool call, so a world-model program cannot survive between decisions. `solution/kaggle/anim_overlay/apply_workspace.py` (persistent bounded memory plus a re-executed prelude) was BUILT on 2026-08-18 with two offline self-checks and NEVER BENCHMARKED, because its push died on an HTTP 409 and was never retried. It targets the Anim tree and needs porting to q38.
what_is_NOT_adoptable: Twin's published system: needs an authenticated frontier CLI and cost 91.4h of wall clock for 25 games against our 9h budget.
Retrodict: no license, so it cannot enter a prize-eligible submission.
Prime Agent as shipped: TypeScript, and the one person who ported it to Kaggle sits at rank 568 with 1.14.
Rebasing onto any public notebook: every public-notebook author sits BELOW us with 3 to 8 times our draws.
